name: Fairchild 24 Argus
summary: Four-seat, high-wing prewar and wartime tourer (and USAAF UC-61 Forwarder / RAF Argus) with a roomy cabin, produced from 1932 into the late 1940s. Some have a radial nose, others an inverted inline engine.

wings: High wing braced by one strut per side
engines: Radial engine with a blunt cylindrical nose, or an inverted inline engine with a tapered nose
fuselage: Deep four-seat cabin with a large windshield
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel
tail: Rudder and fin revised to a more graceful shape in 1938

tellTales: Four-seat high-wing with a long glass cabin and a tailwheel
Blunt radial nose or sleek inline nose over a strut-braced wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The Fairchild 24 has an older, deeper cabin and either a radial or an inline nose; the Stinson 108 has a flat-six nose and a curvier tail.
The Fairchild 24 has a larger, deeper cabin and a sloping nose; the 170 is a smaller, slimmer all-metal fuselage with flat spring-steel gear.
The Fairchild 24 is older and larger with a longer glazed cabin; the Sedan is a squarer fabric aircraft with all-metal wings and a flat-six engine.
The Fairchild 24 has a smaller radial or inline nose and a strut-braced wing; the 195 has a big radial in a deep cowl and a strutless wing.
